component_records.title: Program mobilisation and project management
component_records.description: A mobilisation plan takes the contract from the January 2026 start to first cohort launch, with a monthly timeline covering curriculum development, recruitment, training delivery and placement through completion of internships or full-time jobs by the first cohort. A named program director and project management office run the schedule, risks, ESD status reporting and change control, and the plan states the proposed training duration, cohort size and whether the program runs in the academic year or summer to align with employer internship cycles. The component also sets out the organisational capacity and strategy to run Track A and Track B simultaneously where both are awarded, and the proposed definition of low-income and recruitment targeting for each track. It carries the obligation to perform in a timely and professional manner against the contract, to warrant that services meet applicable professional standards, and to correct at no charge services that fail to meet those standards and produce obvious or patent errors. It also commits to continuing performance as modified after any Corporation change order and to asserting any price or time adjustment claim within 30 days of written notification of change.

component_records.title: Curriculum design and industry-informed content
component_records.description: The administrator builds an online AI curriculum developed with input from leading researchers and industry experts, with learning milestones set against employer technical skill requirements, mentorship and real-world machine learning projects. The curriculum is maintained through a standing employer and expert review cycle so content stays current and aligned with employer demand, and the proposal names the industry experts the administrator partners with. The design states the credentials awarded on completion and the evaluation metrics used to measure participant skill attainment during training. Track A content is built around the skills leading New York technology companies screen for in internship candidates; Track B content is built as an accelerated bootcamp alternative to a traditional degree, with an immersive schedule deliverable part-time or full-time. The component also describes how the administrator delivers substantive, skill-based, college-level or accelerated immersive training in AI, and how AI Prep funding expands and maintains the quality of similar programming the administrator already runs.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment and application assessment
component_records.description: A targeted outreach and recruitment strategy recruits low-income matriculating undergraduates for Track A and low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment for Track B, prioritising New Yorkers currently underrepresented in the tech industry who cannot reasonably access training on their own. The strategy covers unemployed, underemployed and underrepresented New Yorkers, sets out the service area and residency rules, and states how the administrator defines low-income and verifies it. A program application and evaluation process screens applicants against the proposed eligibility definition, which is anchored on Pell Grant eligibility or in receipt of a Pell Grant, with any alternative definition justified in the proposal. Needs assessments at intake identify each participant's barriers to success and route them to the supports they need. The component also describes the administrator's existing work with college students and with low-income individuals, including numbers served and supports provided, and the additional participants AI Prep funding allows it to serve.

component_records.title: Training delivery, stipends and wrap-around supports
component_records.description: The administrator delivers and manages the AI training program for both tracks, running cohorts on the stated schedule with attendance, progress and completion tracking. Every participant receives a stipend at the proposed stipend level, and wrap-around supports include mentorships and career coaches with industry expertise plus success coach staff who address barriers to trainee completion, such as transportation assistance and other supports described in the proposal. Professional development support runs throughout training, covering interview preparation, workplace norms and portfolio building. The component states the proposed stipend level and other supports offered, and is sized to serve a minimum of 250 participants with capacity above 400, with over 50 percent of participants low-income. It also describes how the administrator currently measures and reports program success and the annual estimates it commits to for participants served, low-income completion percentage and placement rate.

component_records.title: Employer partnerships and placement services
component_records.description: An employer partnerships function cultivates and maintains relationships with leading New York State technology companies, both to inform curriculum content and to generate paid internship and full-time job opportunities. The team helps Track A students secure paid internships that let them apply their AI skills in real-world settings and build networks leading to full-time roles, and provides Track B participants with full-time job connection support in AI-related fields. The component describes how the administrator coordinates with individual employers to place participants, and carries the partner employer letters committing to paid internships or full-time employment for graduates. It also describes the administrator's existing New York market work and its partnerships with nonprofits and New York colleges and universities, and sets the placement targets that underpin the majority-of-graduates placement outcome.

component_records.title: Participant data platform and ESD reporting
component_records.description: A hosted participant management and reporting platform captures the data points ESD specifies, with the definitive list fixed at contract negotiation and the platform configured to add fields without rework. At minimum it records the number of applicants and the percentage that are low-income, the number of participants who enroll and the low-income percentage, the number who complete the program and the low-income percentage, the paid internship placement rate and the share of placements for low-income students, the full-time job placement rate and the share for low-income individuals, the participating colleges and universities, and the participating employer partners. The platform produces the monthly and on-request extracts ESD requires, with a defined reporting schedule and turnaround, and holds the audit trail behind each reported figure. It is built to the ESD IT Security Standard Brief in Appendix A, and the administrator confirms the security controls it will apply before go-live.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost governance
component_records.description: The price proposal is built line by line within the $2M per track and $4M combined cap for the total contract period, mapped to the program duration and broken down by period. It carries staff salary and benefits as a cost category with job title, named employee where known, hourly or annual rate, fringe rate, percentage of time and cost to contract, and it carries wraparound supports and the proposed participant stipend level as a separate cost category. Other than personnel services costs are listed on separate lines with cost to contract and number of each item, covering curriculum development and implementation, marketing, events, training materials, equipment, software, insurance and transportation assistance. Indirect costs are excluded entirely, and the extent of any cost matching is shown in the budget template. The component also records that all costs of responding to the RFP are borne by the respondent.

component_records.title: Firm qualifications, staffing and lead-respondent structure
component_records.description: The bid is led by one designated lead organisation that holds the contract and is accountable for the proposed programming, with any team members and subcontractors named in the proposal together with their scope and value so the subcontracting is disclosed up front. Key personnel are named with one-page resumes, and the staffing plan commits assigned staff to the project through completion, with immediate notification to ESD of any proposed staff change and a summary of the substitute's experience plus an interview opportunity before ESD approves or disapproves the change. The component also confirms that assigned staff are subject to ESD approval, that all staff and subcontractor staff hold the qualifications, training, licences and permits required in New York and are legally entitled to work there, and that the firm and its people possess the experience, knowledge and character needed for their duties.
